correctness.rationale: For k>=3 the complete squares split disjointly into odd squares congruent to 1 (mod 8) and four times squares of depth k-2. The extra transform is supported on exactly eight frequencies; its even and odd classes have values c_k and d_k before adding the eighth-root phases. Summing their absolute differences gives the two-step radical recurrence, including k=4 and explicit depths 1,2,3. A convolution-kernel norm identity proves sharpness. The limiting ratios c_k/h_k->1/3 and d_k/h_k->-1/6 give the radical constant; a 2-Lipschitz bound gives |Delta_k-C|<=80/(3*2^k) and parity-dependent convergent offsets with explicit tails. The separate FFT checker passes all Fourier coefficients and Parseval at k=1..12; finite tests are supportive only.

value.rationale: The complete square residue indicator is a canonical arithmetic idempotent Fourier multiplier; its ℓ1/ℓinfty operator norm is a natural sharp amplification invariant. In characteristic two odd squares form an additive coset modulo eight; a nonobvious eight-frequency cancellation produces a new explicit nested-radical slope, exact two-depth increments, and distinct parity-offset limits with effective error. This completes the missing dyadic case rather than merely computing a small table or renaming a known odd-prime formula. Stangl count alone does not determine the norm.
